title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 60-63): Grothendieck is making explicit the fundamental groupoid of the thrice-punctured sphere Σ* = P^1 − {0,1,∞}. Its base 'points' are simply connected regions forming an orbit under the full real-symmetry group Γ = S_3 × {1,τ} (order 12; τ is complex conjugation). The sphere is cut by the real line into two hemispheres, ω ∈ {+,−}, with centres P_±. The real line is cut by 0,1,∞ into three intervals with midpoints Q_i. Further marked points R_i^ω and S_i^± lie on the barycentric-type subdivision. The regions Σ̃_r are permuted simply transitively by Γ. Each gives a 'base region' with a fundamental group π_r and an épinglage Ψ_r : π_{0,3} → π_r (formula (42) on the previous page).

This page:
(1) A point R_i^ω, indexed by r = (i,ω), corresponds to a region of T (presumably one of the six half-triangles cut out on the hemispheres). It lies in exactly two regions D̃_r, matching the two regions of (T,Σ) that extend r. Hence it lies in exactly two of the twelve regions Σ̃_r that contain R_i^ω as an interior point. In the standard region, R_0^+ is interior while R_0^− and R_1^− lie on the boundary.
(2) An orientation of Σ is a marked element ϖ_+ of the Z/2-torsor ϖ = ω ∧ ε (product of the 'hemisphere' torsor and the torsor ε). Equivalently, it is an isomorphism of torsors ω ≃ ε. With it, each R_i^ω singles out a preferred ε, namely the one with ω ∧ ε = ϖ_+. Geometrically, the boundary orientation P_+ S_0^+ R_0^+ Q_∞ P_+ of the region D̃_r agrees with ϖ_+.
(3) Consequently each R_i^ω gets a canonical, orientation-dependent isomorphism (43) Ψ_i^ω : Π_{0,3} → π_1(Σ̃, R_i^ω), obtained from Ψ_r through the transition isomorphism of the simply connected region containing R_i^ω.

The next page uses this to compare Ψ at the two points R^ω, R^{ω'} joined through Q_i by a path b̃_i^ω. The result is formula (45), b̃(Ψ_i^ω(x)) = Ψ_i^{ω'}(τ_∞(x)). This is the explicit bookkeeping needed for a Γ-equivariant presentation of the genus-0, 3-point fundamental groupoid, as input to the 'Galois action on Teichmüller' programme.
errors: No mathematical error is visible. The numbering '(93)' is almost certainly '(43)', given (42) on the previous page and (44) on the next.
The claim that exactly two regions Σ̃_r contain R_i^ω as an interior point is plausible from the figure, but cannot be fully checked without the precise definition of T and D̃_r.

ideas.what: Fundamental groupoid with base points taken as simply connected regions forming a Γ-orbit (Γ = S_3 × Z/2 acting on P^1 − {0,1,∞}), with transition isomorphisms between them
ideas.modern_name: fundamental groupoid with a symmetry-stable set of base points / tangential-type base points (as in the Teichmüller groupoid, Lochak-Schneps, Nakamura)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse, 1984); developed by Ihara, Drinfeld (1990), Nakamura, Lochak-Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (§ on the Teichmüller tower and base points stable under the symmetry group)

ideas.what: An orientation viewed as a marked element of the product torsor ϖ = ω ∧ ε, giving an identification ω ≃ ε and hence canonical épinglages Ψ_i^ω : Π_{0,3} ≅ π_1(Σ̃, R_i^ω)
ideas.modern_name: orientation torsor; choice of base-point isomorphisms (épinglages) for the profinite/discrete free group of rank 2

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful bookkeeping of base-point identifications for the Γ-symmetric groupoid of P^1 − {0,1,∞}. The idea is known from the Esquisse and the later Drinfeld/Ihara/Lochak-Schneps literature, and nothing new is claimed on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 1: 'R_0^{ω}' should be read as the general point R_i^ω; the marginal insertion is 'qu'on va écrire R_i^ω, équivaut à' with r=(i,ω) written underneath.
'les deux autres points R : par R_0^+' — likely 'les deux autres points R que R_0^+ (qui est intérieur), soit R_0^− et R_1^−'.
'donc un iso ϖ ≃ ε' should read 'ou encore un iso \underline{ω} ≃ \underline{ε}', since a marking of ϖ = ω∧ε is an isomorphism ω ≃ ε.
'π_1(Σ̃, R_i^ω) ≃ Π_{0,3}' is written in the manuscript as 'π_1(Σ̃, R_i^ω) : Π_{0,3}' (':' used for ≃).
The struck-out word before 'D̃_r' in 'la région ... D̃_r' is a crossed-out 'Σ̃_r' (consistent with the transcription).
